brief_intent.critique: The main menu is incomplete and the hero is compromised. The brief requires four distinct menu options (Summon / Roster / Battle / Grind) presented as cards or buttons. Only two are visible: a 'Summon' button and a 'View Roster' button in the hero, plus two cards cut off at the bottom of the viewport. expressiveness.critique: The screen leans on a single, safe 'dark navy + gold' mystical trope, so the mood reads as a generic fantasy dashboard rather than a distinct spirit-summoning world. The hero's geometric sigil is the only truly authored element; everything else is flat and uniform. The menu cards at the bottom are near-identical dark rectangles with a small icon and a pill label, offering zero visual differentiation between Summon, Roster, Battle, and Grind—this is the classic 'uniform card' failure that flattens the four very different game roles. Contrast is timid: the secondary 'VIEW ROSTER' button and the stat row (Total Power / Spirits / Win Streak) are low-contrast gray that recedes into the background, and the 'COMMAND / THE SANCTUM' section header is small and muted, so the page lacks a second strong focal moment. The starfield background is a thin scatter of dots with no depth, texture, or atmospheric layering, so the 'atmospheric hero area' feels empty rather than alive. Typography is competent but anonymous—there is no display face with character, and the body copy is a plain sans that doesn't evoke the occult/ritual theme. Color emphasis is monochromatic (gold on dark) with no secondary accent to signal different spirit types, danger, or rarity, so there is no visual vocabulary beyond 'expensive gold.'
expressiveness.suggestion: Give each of the four menu cards a distinct identity tied to its role: Summon as a glowing, animated summoning-circle with a pulsing gold core and a '500g/pull' cost badge; Roster as a grid of small spirit sigils/portraits with a '128/240 bound' counter; Battle as a sharper, angular card with a crimson/ember accent and a crossed-blades or arena motif; Grind as a textured, rune-etched card with a progress bar. Differentiate by shape (rounded vs. angular vs. hexagonal), accent color (gold, teal, ember-red, bone-white), and iconography so the four paths are instantly distinguishable. Build a real atmospheric hero: layered depth with drifting mist, floating ember/spirit particles, and a faintly rotating outer ring on the sigil so it feels like a living ritual rather than a static logo. Introduce a secondary accent color (e.g., spectral teal or ember orange) to break the gold-on-navy monotony and to encode meaning—rarity, danger, or spirit affinity. Promote a second focal moment by enlarging 'THE SANCTUM' header and adding a subtle animated divider or rune line, and lift the stat row with small icon glyphs and a touch more contrast so it reads as crafted data, not placeholder text. Swap the anonymous body sans for a characterful display face on the title and section headers (something with sharp, occult or engraved qualities) while keeping a clean readable face for body copy, to give the screen a signature typographic voice.
